summary: US-P4: The sale charges the resolved price, and the reservation records why
description:
**As** a buyer, **I want** the price I was quoted to be the price I am charged, **so that** a rule change mid-checkout never moves the number under me — and **as** the organizer, I want to be able to prove afterwards which rule produced it.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-151 (resolution + provenance exist)

Closes the epic by putting the hierarchy on the money path. Today `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go` reads catalog's `/internal/ticket-types/{id}` and takes `price.amount` verbatim; after this story it takes the **resolved** price and persists the provenance alongside the reservation.

**⚠️ Money path.** Anticipated and in scope for this ticket — but the plan must say explicitly which existing money invariants it preserves.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Commerce's reserve path sources `unit_amount` from catalog's rules resolution instead of the raw ticket-type price. With **no rules defined the behaviour is byte-identical to today** — the existing commerce and smoke tests stay green unmodified, and that is the regression proof.
- [ ] The reservation persists the **provenance** of the price it was created with (winning rule id + scope level + active tier), so a completed order can be traced to the rule that priced it.
- [ ] **The quote is pinned to the hold**: the price resolved at reserve time is the price checkout charges. A test changes the rules between reserve and checkout and proves the reservation's amount does not move.
- [ ] Resolution failure **fails closed** (ADR-028): a malformed, drifted, or unreachable resolution response aborts the reserve with an error — it never silently falls back to the base price. Note the distinction the test must encode: *no rule matched* is a valid 200 answering with the base price; *could not resolve* is not.
- [ ] Money stays integer minor units end to end (ADR-001); the existing overflow guard on `unit_amount × quantity` still holds for a rule-supplied amount.
- [ ] The commerce operation is exercised through the running stack in the smoke suite (ADR-030 — commerce **is** in the happy-path coverage gate, unlike catalog), and OpenAPI/`api-types.gen.ts` are regenerated and committed before the gate runs.

Quality gates: `make check` green (lint + unit + integration, mirrors CI); contract tests for any touched service boundary (OpenAPI drift check, ADR-009); public-read stories declare their ADR-004 TTL tier with rationale; entities `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002); money is integer minor units + ISO-4217 code, floats banned (ADR-001).

objective.note: A pricing hierarchy nothing sells through is inert; this is the ticket that makes TKT-5 real, and it makes the sale auditable.

scope.note: IN: reserve-path price sourcing, provenance persistence, quote pinning, fail-closed. OUT: repricing on exchange/refund (TKT-9), fees (TKT-6), cart/multi-item (TKT-8), storefront display of provenance.

uncertainties.note: Whether provenance is a column set or a jsonb blob on `reservations` is a Planning-time call; both are reversible within one migration.

dependencies.note: blocked-by TKT-151. Runs after TKT-152 in this epic's sequence, but does not depend on it — the pinning AC holds whether or not tiers exist.

approach.note: Swap the catalog call in commerce's reserve handler for the resolution endpoint; new commerce migration adds provenance columns to `reservations`; the pinning AC is proven at the API test seam with a fake catalog, plus the smoke suite end-to-end.

first_slice.note: One vertical path: reserve → resolved price → persisted provenance → checkout charges the pinned amount.

success.note: Epic COS-1's 'visible provenance' becomes durable, not just readable.

context_memo.note: Baked below; governingAdrs resolved from docs/adr/ at 2026-07-30 and to be re-resolved at claim time.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code — floats are banned on money paths.
Every money mutation flows through the append-only journal; every price/fee decision resolves through the rules hierarchy (TKT-5) once it exists.

governingAdrs.why: DID NOT EXIST when this mémo was baked. §6 is the load-bearing part for this ticket: catalog is the SINGLE authority for the rule-resolved unit price, and commerce consumes resolved_price WITHOUT recomputing it. §5 is the provenance shape to persist — frozen deliberately across TKT-151/152 so snapshots span one format.

AMENDED by ADR-036 on the pricing row. The mémo's original entry ('commerce owns pricing evaluation') is now WRONG for this ticket. Commerce owns sale-time COMPOSITION — price + fees + promos + taxes into an order total — not resolution.

Fail closed. A resolution response commerce cannot validate must abort the reserve, never degrade to the base price. Note the distinction the tests must encode: 'no rule matched' is a valid 200 answering with the base price; 'could not resolve' is not.
The claim/hold transaction is inventory's. Commerce supplies unit_amount to /holds; do not move pricing into the contention path.
The checkout journal protocol governs what commerce records at checkout. Provenance is added ALONGSIDE journalled facts, never in place of one.

Checkout recovery: reserve→checkout is resumable, so anything persisted at reserve time must survive and be RE-READ on the recovery path rather than re-derived — which is also what makes the quote pinning real.
Commerce IS inside the smoke happy-path coverage gate (unlike catalog). A new or changed documented 2xx operation must be exercised through the running stack or the suite fails.
Integer minor units end to end; the existing overflow guard on unit_amount × quantity must still hold for a rule-supplied amount.
Regenerate and COMMIT openapi_gen.go / api-types.gen.ts before the gate.
A commerce migration runs out-of-band via that binary's migrate subcommand.
If the plan calls the stored provenance auditable: name the adversary. It is honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence — ADR-036 §3 has the wording to reuse.

reference.summary: The seam to change: `reserve()` in services/commerce/internal/api/server.go calls `/internal/ticket-types/{id}` and uses `o.Price.Amount` for both the hold and the reservation row.
`reservations.unit_amount` / `total_amount` are the columns the resolved price lands in (commerce migration 0001).

TKT-154 records two pre-existing ticket_types gaps (price_amount unbounded, currency case) that make a legal row unreturnable by a contract-declared endpoint. Not this ticket's to fix, but the reserve path reads that row.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-153 (⚠️ money path)

**Gate 1 waived** (epic TKT-5's `kind=claim`). Last child of the epic; TKT-151 (its only blocker)
and TKT-152 both closed.

**Selection reason.** The only remaining claimable ticket, and deliberately taken **last**: it is
the one that puts the pricing model on a real sale, and it is better done against a finished model
than a half-finished one. TKT-152's windows now exist, so the provenance TKT-153 persists is the
final shape rather than one that gains fields a ticket later.

**Not `risk:low`, and this is the ticket where the run's stop conditions get their real test.**

#### The money-path trigger, and why it does not fire

The run's instructions say to stop if implementation would touch **money paths** *"in a way the
ticket and plan did not anticipate"*. This ticket changes how a sale is priced — that is a money
path by any reading. It does **not** trip the condition, because it is the anticipated one:

- the epic's decomposition named it as a money path and flagged it as concern 2 in the readiness
  verdict, before any code existed;
- the ticket's own ACs are written around the risk — *"with no rules defined the behaviour is
  byte-identical to today, and the existing commerce and smoke tests stay green unmodified"* is the
  regression proof, stated up front;
- ADR-036 §6 already decided the boundary this change respects.

**What WOULD trip it, and where I will stop:** pricing work spilling into payment
authorization/capture, the settlement ledger, the NF525 journal, or the refund/exchange paths. None
of those is in scope, and if the implementation starts reaching for them I stop and report rather
than widening a money-path diff on my own authority.

#### Context-mémo revalidated at pickup

Baked at decomposition (`capturedAt: 2026-07-30`). Everything material has changed since: **ADR-036
now exists** (it did not when this mémo was written) and has been amended three times; **ADR-002 was
amended** by it on exactly the row this ticket depends on. `governingAdrs` rewritten below.

The mémo's original ADR-002 line said *commerce owns pricing evaluation*. **That is now wrong in the
direction that matters most for this ticket** — catalog resolves the unit price; commerce composes
the order total and consumes `resolved_price` without recomputing it.

#### Where this ticket's ACs stand

**Unchanged.** Unlike TKT-151 and TKT-152, no AC needed re-syncing: this ticket was written against
the sale path, and nothing the spike or the two catalog stories decided contradicts it. The one
sharpening worth noting is that "provenance" now has a concrete, frozen shape (`PriceResolution`),
so *"persists the provenance"* means storing that object rather than inventing a format.

Branch: `TKT-153-sale-uses-resolved-price`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — TKT-153

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (config.models.plan), codex companion `task`, read-only, effort
`high`, at HEAD `546c1e5`. The brief carried the money-path warning and its explicit out-of-scope
list, ADR-036 §6, the three shipped code seams, and TKT-154 as a known-adjacent defect not to fix.

---

No files were modified. This plan is based on the merged TKT-151/TKT-152 code, especially `ResolveTicketTypePrice`, `SelectPricingRule`, `reserve`, `staffSale`, inventory’s price-bearing idempotency fingerprint, and commerce recovery’s reads of `reservations.total_amount`.

Production scope stops at catalog reads, the inventory hold request, and commerce reservation persistence. It does not change payment authorization/capture, settlement, the NF525 journal, refunds, exchanges, or any payment production file. The smoke test may observe the existing `payment_operations.request_amount` to prove what checkout charged.

## 1. Definition of Done

- `POST /reservations` obtains identity and slot context from the existing credentialed internal catalog read, but obtains all money exclusively from `GET /ticket-types/{ticketTypeId}/price-resolution`.
- `resolved_price.amount` and `.currency` feed:

  - inventory’s `unit_amount` and `currency`;
  - `reservations.unit_amount`, `total_amount`, and `currency`;
  - the reservation response’s `amount` and `currency`.

- Commerce never applies the winner action or otherwise recomputes the price.
- The full validated `PriceResolution` object is stored as a JSONB snapshot. The common trace fields—resolver version, winning rule ID, scope level, or fallback reason—are generated projections from that immutable snapshot.
- A completed order is traceable through `orders.reservation_id → reservations.price_resolution_snapshot`, without consulting the current catalog rule row.
- Checkout and recovery continue reading the persisted `total_amount`; neither calls catalog.
- A same-key reserve replay after a rule change returns/reuses the first persisted quote and does not re-resolve catalog.
- Invalid, drifted, unreachable, or non-200 resolution results stop before inventory and persistence. A valid `winner:null` plus `fallback_reason:no_eligible_rule` remains a successful base-price answer.
- The existing `resolved_amount × quantity` overflow guard remains before multiplication.
- Existing no-rule commerce and smoke assertions remain unchanged and green.
- `convertOperational` and group draw-down remain behaviorally unchanged and explicitly outside this ticket.
- Contract documentation is sharpened to name the full snapshot obligation; generated Go/TypeScript artifacts are regenerated and committed before `make check`.
- `make check` passes.

## 2. Files

Planned files, one per line:

- `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` — state explicitly that commerce persists the complete `PriceResolution` snapshot and consumes only `resolved_price`.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` — regenerated catalog contract comments/types.
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts` — regenerated from the catalog contract.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts` — regenerated from the catalog contract.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/catalog_pricing.go` — strict consumer-side DTO decoding, semantic validation, and the unauthenticated catalog resolution call.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/catalog_pricing_test.go` — focused reserve-price, fallback, fail-closed, auth, and overflow tests.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go` — public reserve orchestration, persisted-quote replay, canonical reload after `ON CONFLICT`, and snapshot insert.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/migrations/0006_price_resolution_snapshot.sql` — reservation provenance snapshot and generated trace projections.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/migration_smoke_test.go` — v5→v6 upgrade, legacy-row, projection, constraint, and guarded-down tests.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/recovery_smoke_test.go` — characterize that recovery claims carry the reservation’s already-pinned total.
- `smoke/checkout_test.go` — additive running-stack rule-price, provenance, replay, and checkout-pinning scenario.

Not planned for modification: commerce’s OpenAPI response shape, `services/commerce/internal/api/openapi_gen.go`, catalog resolver/store logic, inventory production code, or any payments/access production file.

## 3. TDD order

The first production-facing red test is:

`TestReserveUsesCatalogResolvedPriceForInventoryHold`

Its fake catalog returns:

- raw internal offer price: `1250 EUR`;
- public resolution: winner price `900 EUR`.

While red, it asserts:

- commerce requests `/ticket-types/{id}/price-resolution`;
- the public call carries no `X-Internal-Token`;
- the existing `/internal/ticket-types/{id}` call still carries the token;
- inventory receives `unit_amount: 900`, not `1250`.

The inventory fake returns 409 after capturing the body, so this test needs no database. It fails against the current implementation because no resolution request occurs and inventory receives `1250`.

Then, before implementation:

1. `TestReserveAcceptsNoEligibleRuleFallback`

   Valid 200, explicit `winner:null`, `fallback_reason:no_eligible_rule`, and `resolved_price == base_price`; inventory receives the base amount.

2. `TestReserveFailsClosedOnInvalidPriceResolution`

   Table cases for malformed/trailing JSON, unknown or missing fields, winner and fallback both present, neither present, invalid enum values, winner/resolved disagreement, invalid money, missing `no-store`, and base-price disagreement with the internal offer. Inventory must never be called.

3. `TestReserveFailsClosedWhenPriceResolutionUnavailable`

   Transport failure and catalog 404/500 produce no inventory request and no base-price fallback.

4. `TestReserveRejectsResolvedPriceQuantityOverflow`

   Uses a contract-valid rule amount whose multiplication by quantity exceeds `int64`; proves the guard applies to `resolved_price`, before multiplication or inventory.

5. `TestMigration0006StoresTheFullResolutionSnapshot`

   Red because migration 0006 and its columns do not exist. It verifies winner and fallback projections from handwritten JSON fixtures.

6. `TestMigration0006LeavesLegacyProvenanceUnknown`

   Migrates a v5 reservation and asserts snapshot/projections are `NULL`, rather than inventing a historical “no rule matched” answer.

7. `TestMigration0006RefusesToDropRecordedSnapshots`

   Pins the guarded down migration.

8. `TestClaimStuckOrdersCarriesPinnedReservationAmount`

   Characterization test: `ClaimStuckOrders` returns `reservations.total_amount`, not a newly derived price. This should be green on current recovery code and protects ADR-016 while reserve changes.

9. `TestCheckoutPinsResolvedRulePriceAndProvenance`

   Running-stack smoke test. It reserves under rule A, installs higher-priority rule B, proves catalog now resolves B, replays reserve, checks out, and verifies the hold, reservation, payment-operation request, and completed-order provenance still contain A’s amount.

Only after the focused tests are green should the untouched existing suites and finally `make check` run.

## 4. How commerce calls catalog

Two catalog reads remain necessary because the shipped `PriceResolution` does not contain `organizer_id` or `performance_id`:

1. `GET {CATALOG_URL}/internal/ticket-types/{id}`

   - Direct service URL, not through the gateway.
   - `X-Internal-Token` supplied.
   - Used only to validate organizer ownership and obtain the inventory `slot_id`.
   - Its raw `price` is not used as the sale price.

2. `GET {CATALOG_URL}/ticket-types/{id}/price-resolution`

   - The public, OpenAPI-declared `resolveTicketTypePrice` operation.
   - Direct service URL.
   - No authentication header; specifically, do not leak the internal credential onto this request.
   - Require status 200, JSON content, bounded body, and `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Commerce validates the complete response before touching inventory:

- `winner` and `fallback_reason` are exactly-one-of.
- On a winner:

  - action is `absolute`;
  - all winner identity/tier fields are present;
  - winner amount/currency equal `resolved_price`;
  - enums, IDs, bounds, candidates, and money constraints are valid.

- On fallback:

  - `winner` is explicitly `null`;
  - `fallback_reason` is exactly `no_eligible_rule`;
  - `resolved_price == base_price`;
  - candidates may be empty or may contain expired/future rules.

- `base_price` must equal the raw internal offer price. This is a fail-closed coherence check across the unavoidable two catalog reads.
- Commerce then consumes only `resolved_price`; it does not derive money from `winner.amount`.

“Could not resolve” means transport/read failure, non-200 status, oversized or malformed body, contract/schema drift, invalid enum or invariant, missing required headers, contradictory winner/fallback state, or disagreement between internal offer base price and resolution base price. These abort before inventory. Transport/non-200 maps to commerce 502; a 200 response that is unusable contract data maps to 500 under ADR-028.

“No rule matched” is not an error: it is the valid 200 fallback variant above.

TKT-154 stays separate. No amount bound or currency normalization is added to `ticket_types`; a base row that catalog cannot return through its declared contract continues to fail closed.

## 5. Migration

Planned DDL:

```sql
-- +goose Up
ALTER TABLE reservations
  ADD COLUMN price_resolution_snapshot jsonb,
  ADD COLUMN price_resolver_version integer
    GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
      (price_resolution_snapshot ->> 'resolver_version')::integer
    ) STORED,
  ADD COLUMN price_rule_id uuid
    GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
      (price_resolution_snapshot #>> '{winner,rule_id}')::uuid
    ) STORED,
  ADD COLUMN price_rule_scope_level text
    GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
      price_resolution_snapshot #>> '{winner,scope_level}'
    ) STORED,
  ADD COLUMN price_fallback_reason text
    GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
      price_resolution_snapshot ->> 'fallback_reason'
    ) STORED;

ALTER TABLE reservations
  ADD CONSTRAINT reservations_price_resolution_snapshot_check CHECK (
    price_resolution_snapshot IS NULL
    OR (
      jsonb_typeof(price_resolution_snapshot) = 'object'
      AND price_resolver_version IS NOT NULL
      AND price_resolver_version BETWEEN 1 AND 2147483647
      AND (
        (
          price_rule_id IS NOT NULL
          AND price_rule_scope_level IN
            ('ticket_type', 'slot', 'series', 'event', 'venue')
          AND price_fallback_reason IS NULL
        )
        OR
        (
          price_rule_id IS NULL
          AND price_rule_scope_level IS NULL
          AND price_fallback_reason = 'no_eligible_rule'
        )
      )
    )
  );

COMMENT ON COLUMN reservations.price_resolution_snapshot IS
  'Validated catalog PriceResolution captured at reserve time; NULL means provenance was not recorded by this reservation path, never no-rule fallback. Honest-writer consistency only.';

-- +goose Down
LOCK TABLE reservations IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE;

-- +goose StatementBegin
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM reservations
    WHERE price_resolution_snapshot IS NOT NULL
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION
      'cannot roll back 0006: reservation price-resolution snapshots exist';
  END IF;
END
$$;
-- +goose StatementEnd

ALTER TABLE reservations
  DROP CONSTRAINT reservations_price_resolution_snapshot_check,
  DROP COLUMN price_fallback_reason,
  DROP COLUMN price_rule_scope_level,
  DROP COLUMN price_rule_id,
  DROP COLUMN price_resolver_version,
  DROP COLUMN price_resolution_snapshot;
```

Why JSONB rather than only discrete columns:

- ADR-036 §5’s provenance is a document: resolver version, evaluation instant, base/resolved money, nullable winner with the complete active tier, all losers with reasons, and fallback.
- A discrete representation either loses candidates and tier fields or requires roughly fifteen nullable columns plus an awkward winner/fallback union.
- JSONB copies the values; it does not retain a foreign-key dependency on the mutable/closable catalog row. Later closure, supersession, or deletion cannot rewrite ordinary application history.
- Generated columns expose the common trace keys without duplicating mutable values or requiring JSON expressions in every support query.
- No GIN or provenance index is added: the trace starts from an order/reservation identity, and no subset-query requirement currently exists.
- Existing rows remain `NULL`; backfilling `no_eligible_rule` would fabricate history. Public reserves created after this change must supply the snapshot. The intentionally unchanged staff paths also remain `NULL`.

The application performs the full OpenAPI/semantic validation; the SQL constraint adds an independent top-level/XOR guard. This is honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence: a commerce DB writer can still replace the snapshot.

## 6. Quote pinning and replay

The pin is structural:

```text
catalog resolved_price
  → inventory hold unit_amount
  → reservations.unit_amount / total_amount / snapshot
  → checkout load(total_amount)
  → payment charge amount + order facts
  → recovery ClaimStuckOrders(total_amount)
```

No checkout or recovery branch calls catalog today; the plan preserves that.

Reserve replay must change because `ON CONFLICT(id) DO NOTHING` is insufficient:

- Reservation ID is derived from organizer plus idempotency key.
- Inventory’s fingerprint includes `unit_amount`.
- Therefore, re-resolving after a rule change would send a different inventory fingerprint and get 409 before commerce ever reaches its no-op insert.

Planned replay behavior:

1. Derive the reservation ID immediately after validating the request.
2. Look for that reservation before catalog resolution.
3. If found:

   - compare organizer, ticket type, and quantity with the request;
   - replay inventory using the persisted slot, unit amount, currency, and quantity;
   - require the returned hold ID to match the stored hold;
   - respond from persisted total/currency;
   - do not call price resolution.

4. If not found, resolve, hold, and insert the snapshot.
5. After `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, always re-select the canonical reservation row and respond from it. A concurrent first writer therefore decides the quote; the loser never responds with its freshly resolved value.
6. Preserve the existing 201 reservation response behavior and response shape.

The smoke test installs rule A at 900, reserves two tickets at 1800, then installs higher-priority rule B at 1400 and proves catalog now returns B. Same-key reserve replay must still return 1800. Checkout then completes, and the test verifies:

- inventory claim `unit_amount = 900`;
- reservation `unit_amount = 900`, `total_amount = 1800`;
- stored snapshot and generated projections identify rule A;
- payments’ existing `payment_operations.request_amount = 1800`;
- rule B remains current in catalog, proving the old amount was not coincidentally re-resolved.

One residual gap must be reviewed explicitly: a crash after inventory commits the first hold but before commerce inserts the reservation leaves no persisted commerce quote. If rules change before retry, inventory rejects the new fingerprint and commerce cannot reconstruct the old quote. Closing that requires either a pre-hold durable quote state or an inventory lookup by organizer/idempotency key—both broader protocol work. This plan does not conceal that existing cross-service crash window.

## 7. Other two callers

`convertOperational` and group draw-down remain out of scope.

They share `staffSale` and the raw `offer.Price` seam, but they are distinct internal sale protocols governed by ADR-023 and ADR-027:

- they carve from pre-existing operational/group inventory commitments;
- they have separate namespaced reservation identities and replay rules;
- moving them would require deciding when a staff conversion is priced and adding provenance semantics/tests for both flows;
- changing their catalog fakes would also violate this ticket’s explicit regression condition that the existing commerce tests remain green unmodified.

Their newly created reservations will have `price_resolution_snapshot = NULL`, which means “this path did not record catalog resolution,” not “no rule matched.” Extending rule-resolved pricing to these two staff sale families should be a separately scoped money-path ticket.

## 8. Regression proof

The proof is deliberately the old tests, not rewritten expectations:

- `reserveCheckout` in `smoke/checkout_test.go` keeps its existing `2500 EUR` assertion for two base-price tickets.
- `TestCheckoutSuccessDeclineAndRecovery` remains unchanged.
- `TestDocumentedOperationHappyPathDrivers` remains unchanged.
- Existing operational-hold and group-reservation tests/fakes remain unchanged.
- Existing inventory idempotency and checkout recovery suites remain unchanged.

With no rules, catalog returns the valid fallback whose `resolved_price` equals the old raw price. The inventory fingerprint, persisted unit/total, response fields/status, and checkout charge therefore remain the same. The only new data is the internal provenance snapshot.

Review should reject the implementation if an existing no-rule assertion has to be edited to pass. After additive tests are present, verify the pre-existing test bodies are unchanged in the diff, run `make generate`, commit generated artifacts, then run `make check`.

## 9. Risks and review focus

Review in this order:

1. **Reserve replay and the hold-before-reservation crash window.** Verify a normal successful replay never re-resolves and that the canonical row—not the fresh quote—drives the response. Decide explicitly whether the residual crash gap is acceptable for TKT-153.
2. **Two catalog reads.** Attack coherence between the credentialed identity read and public resolution. The base-price comparison must fail closed; no raw amount may leak into the hold.
3. **Consumer-side contract validation.** The provider’s response validator can be disabled by configuration, so commerce must independently reject missing fields, unknown enums, winner/fallback contradictions, and malformed 200s.
4. **JSONB truthfulness.** `NULL` must remain “not recorded,” never be interpreted as `no_eligible_rule`; the snapshot must include the full winner tier and candidates, not merely rule ID.
5. **Overflow.** Ensure the division guard is applied to `resolved_price.amount` before multiplication and before inventory.
6. **Fallback with candidates.** All-expired rules produce a valid fallback with losers. Code that accepts fallback only when `candidates` is empty would regress TKT-152.
7. **Scope containment.** Confirm no production payment, settlement, journal, refund, or exchange file changes, and that `staffSale` remains untouched.
8. **Smoke fixture validity.** Because no price-rule authoring HTTP surface exists, the smoke test must insert valid rule rows directly into catalog PostgreSQL and use wide time windows to avoid a flaky boundary test.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan -->
### Plan critique — TKT-153

**Critiqued by `main-agent`** (config.models.planReview). Cross-model invariant holds.

#### Existence check

| Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `reserve` uses `o.Price.Amount` for hold + reservation | ✅ `server.go:153,170` |
| the staff path (`convertOperational` / group draw-down) shares the seam **and also INSERTs into `reservations`** | ✅ `server.go:746,806` — the second insert is the part that makes "leave it alone" a real decision, not a formality |
| latest commerce migration is `0005_psp_recovery.sql` → `0006_` next | ✅ |
| `PriceResolution` carries **no** `organizer_id` / `performance_id` | ✅ — this is the root of finding R1 |
| checkout and recovery read `reservations.total_amount`, never catalog | ✅ |
| `/api/catalog/internal/` is blocked at the edge; the resolution path is **not** internal | ✅ `gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go:30,47` — root of finding S1 |

#### The drafter's best catch

**Idempotent reserve replay would 409 at inventory after a rule change.** Inventory's fingerprint
includes `unit_amount`; commerce re-reads the price *before* reaching its `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
So a replayed reserve would send a different fingerprint and be rejected before the no-op insert
ever ran. Nothing in the ticket said this; it comes from reading inventory's idempotency
implementation. **The fix — read the persisted reservation FIRST and replay from it, never
re-resolving — is what makes "the quote is pinned to the hold" true rather than aspirational.**
Accepted wholesale.

---

#### ⛔ REJECT — 1

**R1. Two catalog reads plus a coherence check, where one read would do.**
The plan needs `/internal/ticket-types/{id}` *and* `/ticket-types/{id}/price-resolution` because
`PriceResolution` carries neither `organizer_id` nor `performance_id`. It then adds a fail-closed
check that `base_price` equals the internal offer's raw price, to catch the two views disagreeing.

That check is a symptom. Two non-atomic reads of the same catalog can legitimately straddle a
`ticket_types` price edit, and then commerce **500s a request that was never wrong** — a
self-inflicted failure on the sale path, in exchange for detecting a disagreement that only exists
because there are two reads.

**Amendment:** add `organizer_id` and `performance_id` to `PriceResolution` (additive, no consumer
breaks — TKT-151/152 shipped days ago and commerce is the first consumer). Then **one** read
suffices: it carries the identity, the slot, the money and the provenance. The coherence check
disappears, the race disappears, and the second round trip disappears from the hot path.

Yes, this widens the diff into catalog's contract. That is the smaller cost: the alternative bakes
a permanent reconciliation between two reads into the money path.

---

#### ⚠️ AMEND — 1

**A1. Verify that a `CHECK` constraint may reference `GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED` columns before
relying on it.** The migration's XOR guard reads `price_rule_id`, `price_rule_scope_level` and
`price_fallback_reason`, all generated. PostgreSQL restricts what may appear in generated-column
expressions and in constraints over them, and the exact rule differs by version. **If it is
refused, express the CHECK directly over the jsonb expressions** — same guarantee, no dependency
on the generated columns. Verify at implementation; do not discover it in CI.

#### 🔒 S1 — SECURITY FINDING, out of scope, filed separately: **the resolution endpoint is publicly routable and publishes future pricing**

Not the drafter's error — it is inherited from TKT-151, and **four review passes across TKT-151 and
TKT-152 missed it**, because each was scoped to a diff and this is an emergent property of two
decisions that were individually fine.

`GET /ticket-types/{id}/price-resolution` is a **declared, non-`/internal/` operation**, so the
gateway proxies it (`main.go:30`); only `/api/catalog/internal/` is blocked. Catalog has no auth in
v1. Its `candidates` array reports every considered rule with **id, scope, amount, priority** — and
since TKT-152, that includes rules that lost with `outside_window_future`.

**So anyone on the internet can read an organizer's unannounced future prices, plus their whole
rule ladder, before they go on sale.** For a platform whose users run on-sales, that is a
commercial disclosure, not a theoretical one.

**Deliberately NOT fixed in this ticket.** Adding a credential to an endpoint is *touching auth*,
and this run's stop conditions name auth work the ticket and plan did not anticipate. TKT-153 does
not need it — commerce's behaviour is identical either way — so the correct move is to file it,
flag it loudly, and not quietly change an auth posture on my own authority. **Filed as TKT-155.**

The plan's instruction to **not** send the internal credential to this endpoint is correct as
written, and stays: leaking a service credential onto a public route would be strictly worse.

#### ✅ ACCEPT

- **K1. JSONB snapshot over discrete columns.** ADR-036 §5's provenance is a document; a discrete
  shape either drops `candidates` and the tier fields or needs ~15 nullable columns plus a
  winner/fallback union. The snapshot **copies values**, so a later rule closure or supersession
  cannot rewrite what a buyer was charged — which is the actual requirement.
- **K2. Generated columns for the common trace keys**, so support queries do not write JSON paths.
  Projections of an immutable snapshot, not duplicated mutable state.
- **K3. Nullable snapshot; no backfill.** Legacy rows and the untouched staff paths stay `NULL`.
  *Backfilling `no_eligible_rule` would fabricate history* — exactly right, and it is also what
  makes leaving the staff paths alone coherent rather than sloppy.
- **K4. Staff paths (`convertOperational`, group draw-down) explicitly out of scope.** They share
  the seam *and* insert reservations, so this had to be decided rather than overlooked. Leaving
  them is defensible for a ticket scoped to the public sale; the plan says so out loud, which was
  the requirement.
- **K5. Replay reads the reservation first** (above), with organizer/ticket-type/quantity
  cross-checks and a hold-id match.
- **K6. The fail-closed taxonomy.** Transport/non-200 → 502; a 200 whose body is unusable contract
  data → 500 (ADR-028); `winner: null` + `no_eligible_rule` → a **valid success** answering with
  the base price. That is precisely the distinction the AC demanded.
- **K7. No GIN index on the snapshot** — the trace starts from an order identity; a subset query has
  no requirement yet.
- **K8. The honest-writer framing**, and TKT-154 left alone rather than "helpfully" fixed.

#### 🔎 Pre-mortem

1. **The regression proof passes because the tests never exercised rules.** *Mitigation:* the
   existing commerce and smoke suites must stay green **unmodified** — that is the AC, and it holds
   the no-rule path byte-identical by construction.
2. **The pin holds at reserve and leaks at checkout.** *Mitigation:* the structural chain — no
   checkout or recovery branch calls catalog, and the characterization test on `ClaimStuckOrders`
   pins that.
3. **A crash between inventory commit and the reservation insert** leaves a hold with no
   reservation. The drafter names this as pre-existing and unchanged; it is, and it must not be
   quietly widened.

#### Verdict

**AMEND** — one rejection (R1: one read, not two), one amendment (A1: verify the CHECK), and one
**security finding filed as TKT-155 rather than fixed**, because fixing it means touching auth.
The draft is the strongest of the four in this epic on the dimension that matters here: it went
and read inventory's idempotency implementation, found the replay defect nobody had specified, and
designed the pin around it.
